style_profile.name: LinkedIn Visual Companion
style_profile.objective: Create a visual asset that reinforces the post's idea and earns attention without repeating the whole post, inventing evidence, or looking like generic AI artwork.

single_image_when: The post has one sharp idea, tension, metaphor, or memorable takeaway.
A single visual can create recognition without needing a sequence.
carousel_when: The idea benefits from progression, comparison, steps, layers, or several distinct takeaways.
The reader gains value by moving through the idea one frame at a time.
format_policy.rule: Choose the format because it improves understanding or attention, not because one format is fashionable. Do not turn a one-point post into a padded carousel.

hard_avoids: generic robot heads, glowing brains, humanoid AI assistants, or neon circuit clichés
floating dashboards, fake software interfaces, fake screenshots, or illegible UI
stock-photo handshake/business-team imagery unless the post genuinely requires people
random decorative technology symbols that do not explain the idea
embedded generated text, letters, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-typography inside AI imagery
invented charts, metrics, screenshots, quotations, or factual claims
visual clutter, multiple competing focal points, or excessive small detail
sensational imagery that overstates the post's actual stakes

rules: Use one visual metaphor or one concrete scene, not a collage of ideas.
Keep any headline/overlay text outside the image-generation prompt so typography can be applied separately.
The generation prompt should explicitly request no text, lettering, logos, or watermark.
Prefer a visual that adds meaning instead of merely illustrating the first sentence literally.
Slide 1 earns the swipe with a clear, useful hook.
Each slide advances the idea; do not repeat the post sentence by sentence.
Use concise slide copy that can be typeset by a deterministic layout layer later.
Keep a consistent visual system across all slides.
Do not ask an image model to render the finished slide typography.
End with a useful takeaway or memorable distinction, not a forced engagement CTA.
